newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine may limit foreign T-bill buys - c.bank head.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine may limit foreign T-bill buys - c.bank head.

text.p: Ukraine may soon implement new limits for foreigners participating in its high-yielding Treasury bill market, the central bank chief said on Thursday.

Viktor Yushchenko told Reuters measures could include limiting yields for foreigners, allowing non-residents to purchase only long-term paper, and limiting the number of banks selling T-bills to foreigners.
"The situation requires strict, special regulations for non-residents which would give them enough motivation to participate on the market but would limit speculation," he said.
"We would want non-residents to buy 12-month bills," he said, adding that new rules -- similar to those of Russia's GKO market -- may be passed soon.

Yushchenko also said the central bank and Finance Ministry were close to agreement on regulation of primary and secondary market buying, and on the necessity of abolishing a secondary market trading tax.

Ukrainian T-bills are issued in three-, six-, nine- and 12-month maturities and usually are auctioned twice-weekly by the central bank for the Finance Ministry. They are traded electronically on the interbank market.
The central bank has estimated that non-residents make up to 80 percent of T-bill market activity. Dealers say CS First Boston, Societe Generale and Credit Lyonnais are active participants.
They say banks in Latvia, Lithuania, Cyprus and Czech Republic are also big buyers since tax treaties with those countries allow tax-free repatriation of T-bill income.
Western economists have said foreign banks are spending hundreds of millions of dollars on the market and Ukraine could not afford to cover its deficit if it excluded non-residents.

Yushchenko said the 1997 budget draft, which was preliminarily approved by parliament in December, foresees raising 3.4 billion hryvnia through internal sources such as Treasury bills. Ukraine also plans a Eurobond issue in 1997.
